Scope: infrastructure over about 6.5 km² of the Fourth Industrial City in Riyadh: roads and tunnels, electrical, telecom, ICT and security networks, potable water and fire-fighting, irrigation, sewage and stormwater networks, and sewage and stormwater pumping stations.

Status at a glance

Progress is measured as physical % complete, weighted by budgeted man-hours. At 23.6% against 29.4% planned, the project is behind by 5.8% (SPI 0.80). It gained 3.1% this week. Earthworks are far ahead of plan, but procurement, the zone network works and the tunnels are behind.

The weekly report forecasts completion about eight months late. The weekly report forecasts completion on 06-Feb-2029, 252 days after the contract completion date of 30-May-2028. The P6 extract in the same workbook gives 13-Feb-2029 with −259 days of total float. The "Complete MV and road works" milestone (30-Sep-2026) has passed with asphalt at 8.0% and the MV network at 0.3% installed.

Open issues and risks

IssueOwnerDetail
Clash with SEC high-voltage cablesContractor / SECHigh-voltage cables of the Saudi Electricity transmission company clash with Road C2. A technical solution was submitted and is awaiting SEC's reply. Rated critical; target 30-Oct-2026.
Clash with SEC medium-voltage cablesContractor / SECMV cables clash with Road C8. SEC's contractor (Pillar) has visited the site and a start-of-work record was signed. Rated critical.
Clash with Green Riyadh servicesContractor / Green RiyadhAn air vent and cathodic protection on Road C8 clash with the works. Coordination with Green Riyadh's contractor is ongoing to get drawings and price the diversion. Rated critical.
Clash with ARAMCO gas linesContractor / ARAMCOWet and dry networks on Roads C8 and RD-L10 clash with two ARAMCO gas lines. ARAMCO approved the technical solutions for telecom, sewage, MV, ICT and LV; coordination continues for the remaining networks. Rated high.
Procurement delaysContractorPurchase orders had to be revised after the design changes, and material prices rose. Orders are now issued and supply is under way. Rated high.
Progress behind planContractorProgress lags the schedule because of the master plan change (Wadi Al-Sulai) and the equipment shortage at the start. Most shop drawings are done and equipment and network crews were increased. Rated critical.

Delay reasons stated in the report: the master layout changed after the Wadi Al-Sulai redesign, which changed the design of all networks; and equipment was short at the start of the project.

Data notes

This report uses only the files uploaded for 19-Oct-2026. Earlier weeks were not used, so there is no S-curve section: the workbook's Physical-Chart Data and EV-Chart Data sheets are empty.

  • The weekly planned progress is negative (−3,650 man-hours, −1.55%), which suggests the plan changed this week. Procurement earned value also fell by 2,055 man-hours.
  • Three completion dates appear in the workbook: 30-May-2028 (Milestones sheet), 06-Feb-2029 (General Information) and 13-Feb-2029 (P6 extract, −259 days float). The P6 extract labelled "last week" gives 17-Dec-2029.
  • Procurement: the presentation shows 85–99% of pipes delivered, but the workbook's Major Quantities sheet shows storm 576 m (1.1%), sewage 720 m (3.2%) and potable water 0 delivered. Procurement man-hour progress is only 5.1%.
  • Invoices: the workbook lists 8 invoices, 71,001,361 SAR gross and none paid; the presentation shows 54,980,525 SAR invoiced and 41,804,647 SAR paid.
  • The contract value of 445,000,000 SAR is called "including VAT" on the Conclusion sheet, but the bill breakdown gives the same total as "excluding VAT".
  • Scope totals differ between sheets: MV 131,104 m (presentation) vs 171,170 m (Major sheet); interlock 42,347 m² vs 46,105 m². The Conclusion sheet also lists a second fill row (3,947,936 m³, 2.9%) that looks like an error.
  • Several summary panels show #REF! or #DIV/0! errors (top issues, safety and quality scores in Codes, chart data). Inspection requests show 720 issued, 700 closed and only 1 pending.
  • The October manual head count (252) repeats September's.
  • Photos are stamped 13-Oct-2026, while the presentation's highlights cover 6–12 Oct. Block BL-23 appears under Zone 07 in one file name and Zone 09 in another. A seventh photo (tunnel interior, 20-Oct-2026) has no stamp and was not used.
  • The P6 update (XER archive) was not converted to readable text, so P6 activity counts and milestone floats are not shown.
